properties.statement:
🛑 NINE TEMPORALFACTS CARRY A `subject_id` THAT RESOLVES TO NOTHING, ACROSS **FIVE DISTINCT BAD IDS** — and `subject_id` is not validated on write, so each became a permanent dangling reference.

    prj:reflow2              5   the Project is `proj:reflow2` (26 facts use it correctly)
    cap:reconcile-artifacts  1
    cap:thin-install         1   capability ids that do not exist — renamed, or never minted
    cap:link-artifacts       1
    cap:gap-to-prompt        1

⚠️ **TWO CORRECTIONS TO THIS NODE'S OWN FIRST DRAFT, both found by measuring rather than assuming, and both make the finding SMALLER and more precise.**

**① IT IS NOT ONE TYPO.** The first draft said nine facts carried `prj:reflow2`. Only five do. **Four point at capability ids that do not exist at all**, which is a different and arguably worse cause: a fact about a capability outlives the capability's id. So this is not an agent's slip, it is a class — pointer properties rot when the thing they name is renamed, and nothing notices.

**② THE DANGLING CASE IS MOSTLY ALREADY DETECTED, AND THE REAL GAP IS ONE LINE NARROWER.** `heal.rs`'s orphan check reasons about exactly this and its comment says so: *"a pointer to a node that no longer exists resolves to nothing and is still reported, which is the dangling case, not the ordinary one."* Measured against the live design: **8 of the 9 ARE caught** — as `orphan_node`.

🛑 **The one that is not: a node with a dangling pointer AND at least one edge.** The orphan check short-circuits on `degree > 0` BEFORE it ever looks at the pointer properties, so a fact that is attached to anything hides its broken subject completely. One fact is in that state today (`fact:reflow2s-black-boxes-hold-no-functions...`). **The better a fact is linked, the less likely its dangling subject is to be seen** — which inverts the usual relationship between connectedness and visibility.

📌 THE CONSEQUENCE THAT MOTIVATED LOOKING: `unclaimed_findings` walks from a session's ChangeEvents to the open observations their changed subjects carry. The `capture-session` skill names this exact case as out of reach — *"an observation whose `subject_id` names a node that does not exist"*. A dangling fact can never be offered as a candidate for closure, however much work is done.

⭐ HOW FIVE OF THEM HAPPENED, on the session that then found this: the agent read an existing fact, copied its `subject_id` convention, and never checked that the id resolved — **in a session that had already corrected three other claims-copied-from-a-neighbour errors.** The pattern reproduced while being actively hunted, which is the argument for a check rather than for care. All five were repaired the same day; the four capability-id ones were not, because repairing them means deciding what each fact is now about.

📌 NOT ESTABLISHED: whether `Snapshot.target_id` and `Question.gap_id` — the other two pointer properties `heal.rs` names — carry the same rot. Nobody has swept them.
